It might confirm a total matches, a file exists, a draft follows your rules or a reply stays on topic. We write the checks with you using your real cases.

desc:
Multi-step AI agents with checks at each stage split a big job into gather, draft, check and send, and verify every stage before the next begins. Ecom Swift LLC designs and builds the staged agent, with the rules at each gate and a tested result.

## Why one big request fails on big jobs

Ask an agent to do a long job in one go and a small early mistake travels all the way to the end. A wrong customer name in step one becomes a wrong invoice in step five, and nobody sees it until the output is already sent. The longer the chain, the more places an error can hide.

Splitting the job into stages gives you places to look. Each stage has a clear input and a clear output, and each can be checked on its own. This is how careful human teams work too: one person prepares, another reviews, and only then does the work go out.

## What is a multi-step AI agent?

A multi-step agent is an agent that finishes one stage, checks the result against a rule, and only then moves to the next. If a check fails, the agent can retry, take a different branch, ask a person, or stop and raise an alert.

A typical shape is four stages: gather the facts, draft the output, check the draft against your rules, and deliver. More complex jobs add branches for different cases, steps that run side by side, and review gates where a person decides.

## How staged checks improve accuracy and cost

Smaller steps are easier for a model to do well. A request that says "find the order, check the policy and write the reply" invites shortcuts. Three focused steps, each with its own instructions, produce more consistent results and are easier to improve one at a time.

Checks also protect your budget. A failed stage is caught early, before later stages spend time and model usage on bad input. And when something goes wrong, the run record shows which stage failed, so repair means fixing one step rather than rewriting the whole agent.

## What a well-built staged agent includes

- A diagram of the stages and the order they run in.
- A clear input and output for each stage.
- A check after each stage, such as a rule, a format test or a comparison with source data.
- A retry rule that tries again once, then stops instead of looping.
- Branches for different cases, such as new customers and repeat customers.
- A review gate where a person approves before the final stage.
- Parallel steps for work that does not depend on earlier results.
- A run record for each stage, so problems can be traced.
- A fallback path for the case where a stage cannot finish.
- Tests on your own examples, not only invented ones.

## How we build it

We start by writing down how the job is done today, step by step, including the informal checks people do in their heads. Those habits become the gates. We then decide where the stages split and what each stage needs to pass on.

Next we build the stages in the platform you use, whether that is an automation tool, a script or an agent framework. We write the check for each gate, test it with good and bad inputs, and wire in the retry and stop rules. You receive the diagram, the written rules and the tested build. The Basic package covers a short three-stage agent. Standard adds branching and a review gate. Premium adds parallel steps, approvals and a sheet that shows every run by stage.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give each stage one job and one clear output.
- Check against source facts, not only against the model's own opinion.
- Stop and alert after a failed retry instead of pushing on.
- Put a person gate before any step that sends or spends.
- Test with real messy examples from your work.

**Avoid:**
- Adding stages that do not catch anything.
- Letting a failed check pass quietly with a warning no one reads.
- Retrying forever on a stage that keeps failing.
- Passing the whole history to every stage when a summary would do.
- Building the full pipeline before one stage works well.

## Who this is for

This service suits a team that prepares quotes, reports or customer replies from several sources and sees errors creep in. It suits a business whose single-prompt agent works on easy cases but breaks on harder ones. It also suits an operations lead who needs a clear record of how each result was produced.

## What we need from you

Send a description of the job, a few real examples including difficult ones, and your rules for what counts as correct. Give us access to the tools and the agent platform as a collaborator, team member or developer user, wherever supported. We never ask for passwords, and the build stays in your own accounts.
